page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c7t.4xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1875.78 and a multi-core score of 15544.16. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 846.98 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 95.55 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 56.68 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 21.07 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning, it achieves 1299.46 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter model, though performance drops to 32.22 tokens per second on a larger 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c7t.4xlarge is its low memory allocation of 2 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local NVMe storage, which limits its utility for memory-intensive databases or high-IOPS local caching. However, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution without resource contention. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or GPU acceleration. It is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate-scale computational tasks.
